texts.arguments: The said order passed by the Civil Judge (Junior Division), Jalandhar has not been challenged by the M/S K.B. Foods vs Punjab State Power Corporation Limited ... on 2 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65847261/ 2 petitioner before any Court. 7. The Counsel on behalf of petitioner has approached this Court by averring that in view of the judgment of this Court in the matter "Mobin Ansari versus Punjab State Power Corporation Limited and others" (2022(4) R.C.R (Civil) 782) as well as the subsequent judgment in the matter of "Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited versus Punjab State Power Corporation Limited and others"(2023(3) R.C.R (Civil)306, the 4 of 33 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:082377 petitioner is entitled to release of electricity connection since he is in an authorized and is in permissive possession of the premises in question under a valid lease agreement executed with him and that he cannot be dispossessed except a due process of law. The denial of the basic amenities to the petitioner cannot be permitted as a mode of seeking eviction of the petitioner from the premises in question as the same is likely to promote illegitimate means for seeking eviction of an occupant of the premises. Additionally, an application was also filed for seeking restoration of the said electricity connection and load which was dismissed by the Civil Court. The petitioner has a remedy available to him either to impugn the said order passed by the Civil Judge (Junior Division), Jalandhar before the Appellate Court or to move an appropriate application for an appropriate M/S K.B. Foods vs Punjab State Power Corporation Limited ... on 2 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65847261/ 3 interim relief of seeking release of a new electricity connection in view of the position in law relied upon by the petitioner and as laid down by this Court. Besides, the head note of the plaint clearly contemplates the change in the electricity connection as well as load and a restrain order was sought by the petitioner apart from a separate application seeking restoration. The claim having been already raised, failure on the part of the petitioner in securing the desired relief from Civil Court would not give a fresh cause of action to elect a different forum for the redressal of the same grievance for which he has failed to secure a favourable order in the suit before the Competent Court. 11. Even otherwise if the contention of the petitioner is considered for the sake of arguments that the bar of Order 2 Rule 2 of CPC would not be applicable, yet, the issue in question would at best relate to release a fresh electricity connection and that as per the provisions of forum and 6 of 33 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:082377 ombudsman regulation, the alternative remedy under Section 42 (5) of the Electricity Act read with Section 42 (7) of the Electricity Act have already been prescribed before a statutory body by the name and style of Consumer Grievances redressal forum and the electricity Ombudsman thereafter.

12. It is evident from a perusal of the above that effective, efficient and expeditious alternative remedies have been provided by the Statute.
However, notwithstanding the same, it has been specifically stated in the writ petition that there is no alternative remedy in Para 18 of petition.
The verification on affidavit states that the same is believed to be correct on the basis of legal advice.
Invariably it is a mis-declaration about alternative remedy and since it is based on the legal advice, consequences thereof befall on the Advocate advising the client.

Once certain declaration are mandated under the High Court Rules and Orders,
it cannot be treated as a worthless mandate.

It casts an obligation on the counsel to make a correct and proper declaration and then justify his reason for approaching the Court 28 of 33 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:082377 notwithstanding the alternative remedy.
